editorial.headline: Commercial Sea Fishing, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 03110 covers commercial marine capture and collection, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block recorded for large-scale risk.
editorial.body:
KBLI 03110 is the marine-capture category for businesses whose work begins at sea. Its core is commercial fishing in ocean and coastal waters: finfish such as tuna, skipjack, sharks and rays; crustaceans such as shrimp, swimming crabs and crabs; molluscs such as shellfish, oysters, squid, octopus and sea snails; and a wider field of marine life that includes jellyfish, sea cucumbers, sea urchins, amphibians, reptiles, seaweed, algae and other aquatic biota. The record also places natural marine collection inside the scope, including natural pearls, coral reefs, sponges, seaweed and algae.

This is not a narrow fish-only line. It is a broad commercial sea-harvesting classification, and the sensitive edge of the category matters. The scope expressly includes capture of protected, CITES-listed or legally restricted marine species and biota where those activities are covered or limited by applicable rules. That list includes whales, dugongs, turtles, dolphins, napoleon fish, seahorses, saltwater crocodiles, hard and soft corals, Banggai cardinalfish, sharks and rays. The editorial point is not that every named activity is automatically simple; it is that the KBLI scope itself is wide enough to hold these marine-capture activities where the applicable legal regime permits or restricts them.

On registration scale, the record is unusually broad: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That means the classification can be used by operators from small commercial fishing setups through to larger enterprises, so long as the activity being registered remains within the sea-capture and marine-collection scope. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. For a foreign-owned company, that is the clean national reading: this activity is not capped below full foreign ownership in the supplied record.

The Bali picture is also clear, but for a different reason than many founder concerns. The record says the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and that it is not blocked by the moratorium. The stated reason is practical: at Besar scale, OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not caught by Bali’s island-wide block on Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. In plain terms, the record does not say that a foreigner is blocked from registering this activity in Bali today. It says the activity is nationally open, allows full foreign ownership, is available across all listed scales, and is outside the Bali moratorium block on the basis recorded here.
